subject: Post-demo: EmberCare evaluation plan — model recommendations & guardrail playbook
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Erin Hill <erin.hill@embercare.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-14T15:08:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: EmberCare evaluation plan — model recommendations & guardrail playbook

Hi Erin — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed evaluation plan so we can move to a short pilot: 

Recap (30 min call)
- Primary use case: triage assistant for care coordinators (summarization + next-action suggestions)
- Key constraints: sub-200ms token latency target for short replies, strict PHI/PII handling, and clear refusal behavior on self-harm/medication advice
- Success metrics: refusal rate on sensitive prompts, factuality on clinical extractions (F1 on gold dataset), and cost per 1k tokens

Recommended models to shortlist (based on your latency/cost profile):
- rw-13b-v2-quant: strong latency/cost balance for shorter prompts, good refusal baseline
- rw-70b-opt: best for complex synthesis when higher latency acceptable (can be used as fallback for long cases)
- rw-7b-lite-emb: for embedding-based retrieval and reranking

Proposed evaluation steps (2 weeks):
1) You share a 500–1k sample of de-identified triage transcripts (or synthetic equivalent).
2) We run the prompt-set (attached: embercare-prompt-set-v1.csv) across the three model candidates.
3) Benchmarks: latency distribution, token cost estimates, refusal/acceptance classification, and clinical extraction F1.
4) Safety/regression checks: run refusal prompts + roleplay tests for sensitive domains (mental health, medication).
5) Deliverable: benchmark PDF + guardrail playbook with suggested prompt templates and rollout thresholds.

Ask: can you provide a de-identified sample by EOD Wednesday (2027-06-16)? Also please share the security contact for transfer method (S3 link/Drive) and any required DPA/NDA notes.

Attachments: embercare-prompt-set-v1.csv (prompt templates & masks)

Next steps suggested:
- If you’re good with this plan I’ll schedule a 45-minute kickoff with Marissa (responsible for evals) and Ben (solutions) to finalize dataset schema and success criteria.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182
From: Erin Hill <erin.hill@embercare.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@embercare.ai>
Date: 2027-06-14T17:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: EmberCare evaluation plan — model recommendations & guardrail playbook

Thanks Sean — really clear plan, appreciate the breakdown. A few quick answers and clarifications: 

- We can provide a 750-record de-identified sample (PHI redacted) via a private S3 link. I’ll coordinate with our data team to get that uploaded by tomorrow afternoon.
- Security contact for transfer and questionnaire is Alex Rivera (cc’d). He’ll confirm acceptable transfer method and any required attestations.
- Timeline looks good; two-week initial run is fine as long as we have the benchmark summary and guardrail recommendations to review the following week.

Question: on the refusal tests — do you include both hard refusal (explicit decline) and soft-refusal (safe alternative suggestion)? For our care flows we need the model to offer next steps rather than only saying “I can’t help”.

Also, can you include a basic evaluation of hallucination risk on discharge-summary style prompts?

Thanks — Erin
Erin Hill
Head of Product | EmberCare
erin.hill@embercare.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Erin Hill <erin.hill@embercare.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T08:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: EmberCare evaluation plan — model recommendations & guardrail playbook

Erin — great questions. To confirm our approach on the evaluation and safety checks: 

1) Refusal taxonomy: we test three behaviors per prompt set sample:
   - Hard refusal: explicit refusal with brief explanation (when user asks for disallowed medical instructions).
   - Soft refusal + signpost: brief refusal followed by safe, evidence-backed next steps (e.g., encourage contacting provider, provide non-actionable resources).
   - Deflection to human: where the model surfaces a handoff suggestion and a summarized context for the human agent.

2) Hallucination tests: we’ll run a targeted discharge-summary probe set (10 templates) and measure entity hallucination rate vs your gold annotations (F1 precision on medications, dates, diagnoses).

3) Guardrail playbook: attached is our working doc (guardrail-playbook-v0.2.docx) and an initial benchmark summary (initial-benchmark-summary.pdf) from a similar healthcare pilot. Key items included:
   - Prompt templates for safe refusals and required context preservation
   - Runtime checks: NER-based PHI filters, prefix-based refusal overrides, and fallback routing rules (rw-70b-opt fallback for complex cases)
   - Rollout thresholds: stop/gate if hallucination increase >5% or safe-refusal failure rate >3%

Operational asks from your side:
- Provide S3 link and one point-of-contact for security review (Alex is fine).
- If you have any legal/DPA requirements for model caching or logs retention, flag them now so we can include explicit config in the pilot.

Proposed next meeting: 30–45 min kickoff Thursday 2027-06-17 10:00–11:00 PT. I’ll send a calendar invite after Erin confirms.

Attachments: initial-benchmark-summary.pdf, guardrail-playbook-v0.2.docx

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
